FN-LM8CAWA-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 439
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Representative Alan Baker
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 05/01/2024
House Bill 439 as reported by the Committee on Education Policy would increase the annual
obligations of local boards of education by an undetermined amount dependent on the travel
costs and course fees for each technology director of a public K-12 school system to attend and
complete certain professional development required by this bill.
Additionally, this bill would amend the K-12 Capital Grant Program to: (1) increase the amount
of the available fund monies used to administer the program to an amount not to exceed 1%; (2)
require that any K-12 Capital Grant Program Fund monies that are unobligated at the conclusion
of the second consecutive fiscal year without an appropriation to revert to the Education Trust
Fund; and (3) allow a K-12 entity that receives grant funds to amend their grant proposal once
within 12 months of receipt of a grant and then return any unobligated funds the Office of the
Lieutenant Governor.
This bill would also repeal the Distressed Institutions of Higher Education Revolving Loan
Program, and transfer any funds remaining in the Distressed Institutions of Higher Education
Loan Program Fund to the Education Trust Fund, to be immediately available for supplemental
appropriation for Fiscal Year 2024. As of April 1, 2024, the balance of the fund was
$29,998,245.70.
Finally, this bill would decrease the obligations of the State Treasurer to administer the
Distressed Institutions of Higher Education Revolving Loan Program and any monies in the
Fund.
